facts.statement: The researchers created a machine-learning tool called THERM-D to continuously and rapidly measure body temperature rhythms in fruit flies.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The study found that the flies' body temperature rhythms match their morning and evening activity patterns and identified the role of a specific group of brain cells.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Roughly half of the brain cells that control the body clock do not contain a protein called CRYPTOCHROME, and their exact job was not fully known before this work.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: By manipulating the brain cells that lack the CRYPTOCHROME protein, the team showed that these cells are responsible for the body temperature increase in the morning.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The research indicates that different groups of brain cells manage the body temperature changes in the morning versus the evening.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The new tool helps explain how specific brain cells control daily temperature cycles and offers a way to study how the body maintains its temperature rhythm.
facts.subject: animals
